description: We have developed a high-fidelity Space Mission Control Dashboard and Architecture Simulator that enables engineers and students to model a futuristic deep-space mission: deploying an autonomous swarm of micro-satellites into a Black Hole's event horizon. The system simulates extreme real-world constraints such as time dilation, high-intensity radiation cascades, and spaghettification. Instead of a traditional recreational game, our platform acts as an interactive system design simulation
summary: Inside the Black Hole is a space strategy game created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The project focuses on a mission towards Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way. Players act as mission commanders and control 5,000 micro-probes to reach the target. They make strategic decisions, manage probes, and face challenges during the mission. The game combines space science, technology, and problem-solving through interactive gameplay. It helps players understand space exploration in an interesting and engaging way. Our team includes Shafaq (Team Lead), Ayesha, Maheen, Tooba, Zukhruf, and Ahtisham. Our goal is to encourage curiosity about astronomy and show how teamwork, creativity, and technology can bring scientific ideas to life.
details:
Inside the Black Hole is an interactive space-mission strategy game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project focuses on the challenges of designing a space mission towards Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole located at the centre of the Milky Way galaxy.
How It Works:
The game allows players to take the role of space mission strategists and command a fleet of 5,000 micro-probes towards Sagittarius A*. Players must make strategic decisions, manage their probes, and plan their mission while considering the difficulties of exploring an extreme space environment. The main objective is to make mission planning an interactive and engaging experience.
Benefits and Intended Impact:
Our project aims to increase public interest in astronomy, black holes, and space exploration. It encourages critical thinking, strategic planning, decision-making, and problem-solving. It also makes complex space-related concepts more approachable for students, learners, and space enthusiasts.
Creativity and Innovation:
The creative aspect of our project is its combination of scientific exploration and strategy-based gaming. Instead of presenting information about black holes through text alone, we provide an interactive experience that allows users to engage with the idea of planning a challenging space mission.
Development and Technology:
The project is presented as a web-based interactive experience and is publicly hosted on Vercel. Development technologies, programming languages, frameworks, and additional software should be documented according to the tools actually used by our team.
Team Considerations:
During development, our team focused on the mission objective, management of 5,000 micro-probes, strategic decision-making, user experience, accessibility, and making the scientific concept engaging and understandable.
The project was developed by Shafaq (Team Leader), Ayesha, Maheen, Tooba, Zukhruf, and Ahtisham. Our shared goal is to combine creativity, teamwork, science, and technology to inspire curiosity about the universe and future space exploration.
